Histogram stretching modifies the intensity range using the formula: $I(x, y) = \frac{I(x, y) - I_{min}}{I_{max} - I_{min}}$, where $I_{min}$ and $I_{max}$ are the minimum and maximum values of the intensity respectively [S3].

The claim states that histogram stretching modifies the intensity range using the formula $I(x, y) = I(x, y) - I_{min} / I_{max} - I_{min}$, where $I_{min}$ and $I_{max}$ are the minimum and maximum values of the intensity respectively. Source [S3] explicitly contains the sentence: 'Histogram stretching modifies the intensity range using the formula: $I(x, y) = I(x, y) - I_{min} / I_{max} - I_{min}$, where $I_{min}$ and $I_{max}$ are the minimum and maximum values of the intensity respectively.' The evidence matches the claim exactly.
supported
Compute the Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) as a sum of PDFs over normalized scalar inputs: $CDF(x_i) = \sum_{x_j < x_i} PDF(x_j)$ [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the CDF is computed as a sum of PDFs over normalized scalar inputs, specifically citing the formula $CDF(x_i) = sum_{x_j < x_i} PDF(x_j)$. Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Mathematically, histogram equalization is performed by introducing a cumulative density function (CDF) as a sum of probability density functions (PDFs) over normalized scalar inputs: CDF(xi) = sum_{xj < xi} PDF(xj).' The evidence directly supports every part of the claim.
supported

Histogram Stretching with Percentile Clipping is a post-processing step to create a balanced RGB image by suppressing high intensity outliers caused by constructive interference phenomena inherent to diffraction [S3].

It further describes 'histogram stretching' as the subsequent step to modify the intensity range. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
